title: PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-agent — A self-improving RLM agent for coding workflows and long-running autonomous tasks.
content:
Documentation • Verifiers • PRIME-RL
Prime Agent is an open-source coding and research agent for general and long-running work. It is designed around two core abstractions:
- The Recursive Language Model (RLM) treats context as variables (prompt-as-a-variable) and tools like recursive subagents as function calls (programmatic tool /sub-agent calling) inside a persistent REPL.
- The Continual Harness stores supplemental prompts, memories, skill descriptions, and reusable subagent specifications as durable state that Prime Agent can refine through small, evidence-backed updates, local to the session by default.
Prime Agent combines a persistent Python control environment with durable harness state, so useful working context and reusable operating patterns can outlive a single chat window.
- Everything is programmatic: a persistent Python REPL is the built-in model tool; file operations, shell commands, tool use, subagents, and context management happen through code.
- Subagents are built in: rlm(...) spawns real child agents for parallel or background work and returns their results programmatically.
- The harness can improve: /refine reviews the current trajectory and can apply small, evidence-backed updates to supplemental harness state. It never rewrites the immutable base system prompt, and recorded snapshots support rollback.
- Skills are executable: skills are importable Python packages, and the built-in skill creator can turn recurring workflows into project or personal skills.
- Sessions run in the background: daemon-backed agents keep running when the terminal disconnects and can be reattached later.
- Agents communicate directly: running agents can exchange messages and orchestrate one another without routing everything through the user.
- Long tasks keep moving: automatic compaction, persistent goals, heartbeats, schedules, autonomous mode, and retained subagents preserve progress across turns and terminal sessions.
Install the latest stable release on macOS or Linux:
curl -fsSL https://app.primeintellect.ai/prime-agent/install.sh | sh
The installer downloads a versioned release, verifies its SHA-256 checksum, installs the prime-agent command, and can prepare the Python runtime used by the agent.
Start Prime Agent from the repository or directory you want it to work in:
cd /path/to/project
prime-agent
On first launch, run /login to choose a subscription or API-key provider. Prime Agent works in the current directory and can run commands and modify files there. Use a disposable clone, clean worktree, or another checkpoint you can inspect and restore.
Warning
Prime Agent executes model-generated Python and project commands with your user permissions. Its worker and kernel processes improve lifecycle isolation and recovery; they are not a security sandbox. Review changes and use trusted repositories, instructions, skills, and extensions only. Run untrusted code or instructions in an external sandbox or restricted environment.
Useful commands:
prime-agent agents                   # Browse running, idle, and saved sessions
prime-agent attach <agent>           # Reattach to a running session
prime-agent --resume [path|id]       # Browse sessions or resume one directly
prime-agent status                   # Inspect background service state
prime-agent doctor [--fix]           # Inspect or repair background services
prime-agent update [--force]         # Update Prime Agent
prime-agent shutdown [--force]       # Stop every agent, worker, and background service
Prime Agent is built for long-running work, especially for evaluations in research. These features are available in the TUI, and when run autonomously.
- Continual Harness: /refine can persist focused, reviewable lessons as supplemental prompts, memories, reusable skill descriptions, or subagent specifications, with recorded refinement history. It does not replace packaging and reviewing new executable skills.
- Direct agent-to-agent communication: running agents and retained subagents can discover one another, exchange messages, and steer active work.
- Daemon-backed continuity: active sessions, Python REPL state, schedules, and subagents keep running when the terminal detaches and can be reattached later.
- Heartbeats and schedules: /heartbeat ,rlm_heartbeat , andprime-agent schedule can re-enter a session periodically or at a specific time.
- Persistent goals: /goal keeps an objective and its progress active across turns until it is completed, paused, or cleared.
- Bounded autonomous mode: /autonomous continues within configured turn, token, and time budgets and can run user-defined quality gates. A passed gate checks only what that gate verifies; reaching a limit does not imply task success.
- Quickstart — install, authenticate, and run a first session
- Usage and CLI reference — commands, sessions, autonomous limits, and output modes
- Long-running and background agents — detach and reattach, goals, heartbeats, and schedules
- RLM programming model — the persistent Python REPL, subagents, skills, and the trust model
- JSON mode and RPC mode — headless automation and integrations
- Skills — install and create reusable capabilities
- Provider setup — subscription and API-key providers
- Architecture overview — daemon, worker, kernel, and persistence boundaries
- Development — build and run from source
Start with a GitHub Discussion for general questions, bug reports, and feature requests. Maintainers promote accepted work into Issues, and pull requests are reviewed from maintainers and vouched contributors.
Read the contribution guidelines for the full process. Report security vulnerabilities privately by following the security policy.
Our agent and TUI is built on top of pi. We thank the authors of pi for their valuable work.
Prime Agent is fully open source and released under the MIT License.

report.summary: Prime Agent is an open-source self-improving coding and research agent combining a persistent Python REPL, recursive subagents, and durable memory for long-running autonomous tasks.
report.background: Most coding agents are designed for short, chat-driven tasks and lose momentum over long horizons. Prime Agent is an open-source research and coding agent from PrimeIntellect based on the Recursive Language Model (RLM) abstraction: context is treated as persistent variables, and recursive subagents are programmatic function calls inside a live Python REPL. A “Continual Harness” stores supplemental prompts, memories, skills, and subagent specifications as durable state that can be updated through small, evidence-backed refinements. It grows out of the PRIME-RL line of work and builds on the pi agent/TUI framework. Released under the MIT License, it targets software development and research evaluation workflows that need to continue in the background across terminal sessions for hours or days.
key_points: Everything is code: Prime Agent’s core model tool is a live Python session in which file edits, shell commands, and subagent calls are written and executed. Because the REPL persists, intermediate variables and results remain available across turns, letting a session accumulate working context instead of restarting from scratch after every chat message.

It uses recursive subagents: the rlm(...) command launches actual child agents that can run in parallel or in the background and return structured results, so complex workflows can be decomposed. Agents can also exchange messages directly rather than routing every step through the user, making multi-agent orchestration practical for long-running work.

The agent can refine itself in a constrained way: /refine reviews the recent trajectory and proposes small, evidence-backed updates to durable supplemental state—such as memories or skill descriptions. It never rewrites the immutable base system prompt, and recorded snapshots enable rollback. That lets useful lessons outlive a single session while keeping core behavior stable.

It is built for long-running autonomous sessions: daemon-backed agents survive terminal disconnects, /heartbeat and schedules can re-enter work, persistent goals keep objectives alive, and bounded autonomous mode enforces turn, token, and time budgets. This moves agents from interactive chat tools toward dependable background workers for evaluations and research.

Security is explicit: Prime Agent executes model-generated Python and shell commands with the user’s own permissions. Its worker/kernel isolation improves lifecycle management and recovery, but it is not a security sandbox. Users are advised to run from disposable clones or clean checkpoints and use only trusted repositories, instructions, skills, and extensions.
report.impact: Prime Agent represents a shift from coding copilots to durable, self-improving agents that can plan, delegate, and refine their own reusable knowledge over long-horizon work. For developers, this may reduce the overhead of autonomous software tasks and research evaluations by preserving context, goals, and learned tactics across sessions. For the AI industry, it highlights a trend toward verifier-driven, evidence-backed self-improvement rather than raw context accumulation. The biggest challenge is safety: because the agent can modify files and run commands with user privileges, teams must adopt sandboxing, disposable environments, and strict review processes before letting such agents operate unattended on production codebases.
report.tools: Watch the Prime Agent GitHub repository and its companion PRIME-RL work on verifier-driven reinforcement learning, along with the pi library it is built on. For practical comparison, open-source agent frameworks such as OpenHands, SWE-agent, and Aider offer different approaches to autonomous coding and are useful for benchmarking long-running agent behavior.
